responses.raw_text: {"no_themes_found":false,"themes":[{"theme_id":"T1","label":"Value of low-key casual spaces","description":"Participants value unassuming, local venues where they can relax, be themselves, and talk without the pressure of high costs, dress codes, or curated vibes.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T002","speaker":"P1","quote":"I think the main thing is it's just... low-key, you know? No one's trying too hard. You can sit there for three hours nursing a couple of pints, chat about whatever — football, work drama, sometimes just mess about — and there's no pressure to be doing something else or going somewhere flashier. It's just a place where you can actually be."},{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"P2","quote":"There's one place I go to sometimes that's got that feel Isaiah's talking about, but it's getting fewer and further between. And when you can't find somewhere like that — somewhere you can just be yourself without it being a whole thing — you end up just... staying in, I suppose."},{"turn_id":"T008","speaker":"P4","quote":"But there's loads of choice, so it's almost harder to just... be somewhere casual, if that makes sense."}]},{"theme_id":"T2","label":"Decline of local community spaces","description":"Speakers note that the closure, commercialization, or geographic dispersion of neighborhood establishments has eroded the availability of accessible local hubs.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T003","speaker":"P2","quote":"Which defeats the purpose of having a local community space, doesn't it?"},{"turn_id":"T004","speaker":"P1","quote":"Like, it's not really a local spot anymore if you've got to drive twenty minutes to get there, is it? You lose the whole casual thing about it. You can't just pop round the corner because you're bored."},{"turn_id":"T007","speaker":"P3","quote":"There's definitely pubs I used to go to that have shut down or turned into something else."},{"turn_id":"T008","speaker":"P4","quote":"It's not like there's one local spot where everyone in your neighbourhood naturally ends up."}]},{"theme_id":"T3","label":"Spontaneous versus scheduled socializing","description":"As local venues disappear, meeting up with friends changes from natural, spontaneous encounters to structured, planned events that require more effort and feel more pressured.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T005","speaker":"P2","quote":"Like, if you've got to plan it and drive somewhere, you're not just casually meeting up. You're making it an event. Which sounds fine, but then you end up doing it less because it's more effort, and then... I don't know, you see your mates less often."},{"turn_id":"T006","speaker":"P1","quote":"But when it's all scheduled, there's more weight to it. You're trying to make it a good night, you're catching up on everything that's happened, it's got to be worth the effort. And sometimes that's actually good, but sometimes it just... it changes what you talk about, how relaxed you feel."},{"turn_id":"T007","speaker":"P3","quote":"You're not bumping into your mates by accident like you might have done if there was something local. And the messaging thing Isaiah mentioned — yeah, that tracks. You message more because you're not just seeing people naturally."}]},{"theme_id":"T4","label":"In-person depth versus digital messaging","description":"While digital messaging keeps friends in constant contact, participants feel it cannot replicate the depth and relaxation of in-person conversations, leaving friendships feeling thinner.","descriptive_prominence":"MEDIUM","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T006","speaker":"P1","quote":"And you're right about the messaging thing — we message loads now, but it's not the same. It's quick updates, memes, whatever. But there's stuff you just wouldn't text about that you'd chat through over a pint, you know? I've definitely noticed friendships feel a bit thinner when it's just that."},{"turn_id":"T005","speaker":"P2","quote":"You're messaging them more but actually hanging out face-to-face becomes this thing that has to be scheduled weeks in advance. I've got mates who've just kind of drifted because of that."}]}]}

{"no_themes_found":false,"themes":[{"theme_id":"T1","label":"Anxiety and paralysis of choice overload","description":"The overwhelming number of food options presented on delivery apps leads to decision paralysis, anxiety, and a persistent fear of making a suboptimal choice.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T010","speaker":"P2","quote":"But when there's that much choice it's almost paralyzing, you know? Like, any decision you make feels like you're missing out on something better."},{"turn_id":"T012","speaker":"P2","quote":"You feel like you're making the wrong call even before you've eaten anything."},{"turn_id":"T013","speaker":"P1","quote":"It's not the choice itself — it's that these apps, they're literally designed to keep you scrolling, looking at more options, reading reviews from random people you don't know."}]},{"theme_id":"T2","label":"Screen-mediated isolation in decision making","description":"Making food choices individually on a phone screen creates a stressful burden of self-justification, whereas choosing as a group is a fast and social experience.","descriptive_prominence":"MEDIUM","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T011","speaker":"P1","quote":"It's not even just about having loads of options, it's that you're doing it on your own, aren't you? On your phone, comparing prices and ratings and looking at photos of the food."},{"turn_id":"T012","speaker":"P2","quote":"Because like, when I'm out with the lads and we're deciding, it's quick — someone says chicken shop, someone else says nah let's get a curry, and you just pick one and move on. No one's stressed about it. But when I'm on my own at home scrolling, I'm like... reading reviews from randoms"}]},{"theme_id":"T3","label":"Loss of independent local businesses","description":"Local, independent food establishments are disappearing and being replaced by chains, leading to a narrowing of genuine choice that is masked by the illusion of variety on delivery apps.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T015","speaker":"P3","quote":"but honestly the issue for me isn't having too many options — it's more that a lot of the decent independent places have either shut or they're changing into chains."},{"turn_id":"T016","speaker":"P4","quote":"So your actual choice has got narrower, but the apps are trying to make out there's more, and it's just... the same stuff repeated."},{"turn_id":"T017","speaker":"P3","quote":"You scroll through Deliveroo and you think, oh there's loads here, but it's just... it's the same chains everywhere, just different names on them sometimes."}]},{"theme_id":"T4","label":"Decline of community and human connection","description":"The shift toward digital food ordering turns what used to be a warm, community-based human interaction into a cold, transactional, and isolated experience.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T017","speaker":"P3","quote":"It's becoming more... transactional. You're ordering through an app from your house, it arrives, you eat it alone probably, and there's no actual connection to anywhere or anyone."},{"turn_id":"T018","speaker":"P4","quote":"It's that all these small interactions, the ones that made a place feel like an actual place, they're just... they're gone. And you don't realise how much you miss them until they're not there anymore."},{"turn_id":"T018","speaker":"P4","quote":"And now it's just... you tap your phone and forty minutes later a driver you'll never meet again leaves it on your step. You don't know who made it. You've got no connection to it at all."}]}]}

{"no_themes_found":false,"themes":[{"theme_id":"T1","label":"Complicity in losing local spaces","description":"Speakers discuss how choosing the convenience of delivery apps over physical venues makes them active participants in the decline of the local places they value.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T019","speaker":"P1","quote":"It's weird because you feel powerless — like, what am I gonna do, not use Deliveroo? — but you're also kind of complicit in killing off the thing you're saying you miss."},{"turn_id":"T021","speaker":"P3","quote":"And this is kind of the same trap — the thing that lets you escape the awkwardness, the social performance of being a bloke eating alone, is the same thing that's killing off the actual human spaces and the connections that go with them."},{"turn_id":"T025","speaker":"P3","quote":"But knowing that choice exists, knowing there's something to lose... I think that does mean something different than if everything was already shut."}]},{"theme_id":"T2","label":"Apps as refuge from social judgment","description":"The participants describe using mobile delivery apps as a way to avoid the social performance, self-consciousness, and judgment of eating alone or ordering unconventional foods in public.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T020","speaker":"P2","quote":"Because you're not actually going anywhere. You're not sitting in a space where someone might clock you, judge you. You're eating at home, or with your mates in someone's flat. There's no... there's no social performance happening."},{"turn_id":"T021","speaker":"P3","quote":"And you're right about the app thing solving it in a way — because you're not actually in the space, you're not being looked at. The choice happens in private, the eating happens in private."},{"turn_id":"T026","speaker":"P4","quote":"If I'm ordering at home, I can get whatever I want without thinking about how it looks. Without thinking about what someone might say."},{"turn_id":"T033","speaker":"P2","quote":"And I think that's actually why the app works so well for this stuff. Because it's not just that you're isolated — it's that you can make choices that would otherwise be readable as statements without anyone actually knowing about it."}]},{"theme_id":"T3","label":"Gendered expectations in food choices","description":"The speakers explain how certain foods, such as salads or vegan options, are policed by peers and carry negative social consequences or feminine connotations for men.","descriptive_prominence":"HIGH","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T026","speaker":"P4","quote":"But if I'm getting like... I dunno, a salad, or something that looks fancy or a bit fussy, there's this wee voice in your head going, is this a bit much? Like, would someone take the piss if they found out that's what I ordered?"},{"turn_id":"T028","speaker":"P4","quote":"Because if you're in a pub full of blokes and you're visibly ordering something they think is soft or fussy, you're not just getting judged quietly. You're getting proper taken the piss out of."},{"turn_id":"T032","speaker":"P5","quote":"But the vegan thing especially — it's not just about being seen eating something. It's about what people assume you're saying about yourself by eating it."}]},{"theme_id":"T4","label":"The erosion of social spaces","description":"Participants discuss how the decline of community venues removes the physical spaces where social pressures could be challenged and authentic connections could happen.","descriptive_prominence":"MEDIUM","quotes":[{"turn_id":"T022","speaker":"P2","quote":"The middle ground isn't gone because it's impossible. It's gone because the places that used to create it — the local spots, the ones run by actual people, the ones where you might bump into someone or just be a familiar face — they've been replaced by chains and apps."},{"turn_id":"T030","speaker":"P4","quote":"So the whole thing where social pressure could shift — it kind of assumes there's still an actual social space where that shifting could occur. And for a lot of people, there isn't. That's the actual trap. It's not about individual willingness. It's about the spaces where anything could change being gutted already."}]}]}
